To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the general boundary conditions for quasiparticle scattering at the interface between diffusive normal metals and superconductors are given by the Usadel equations, with the boundary condition that the normal components of the Green functions are continuous, and that the anomalous Green functions are continuous for a spin-independent interface.

the Usadel boundary conditions for diffusive superconductor/half-metallic ferromagnet/superconductor junctions are the same as for the ballistic case, but with the spin-mixing angle replaced by a spin-mixing matrix.

we derived boundary conditions for the quasiclassical diffusive limit for arbitrary spin polarization of the ferromagnetic material, for any transmission probability and for arbitrary spin-mixing angle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general theory of superconducting proximity effects in diffusive systems.

the development of the theoretical tools needed for a quantitative description of the proximity effects in superconductor/strongly spin-polarized material/superconductor heterostructures in the diffusive regime.
the derivation of boundary conditions for the quasiclassical Usadel theory for diffusive superconductivity in contact with strongly polarized ferromagnetics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have derived boundary conditions for the quasiclassical Usadel theory of superconductors in the diffusive regime for interfaces with strongly spin-p polarized materials, including half-metallic ferro- magnets, for arbitrary transmission probability, arbitrary spin-mixing angle, and arbitrary spin-dependent scattering phases.
our results are of great importance for a proper understanding and description of proximity effects in heterojunctions of diffusive superconductive and ferromagnetic systems.

the Usadel equations for diffusive superconductivity are now well understood in their boundary conditions for any interface, and the theory can be applied in a general and rigorous way to a wide range of systems, including those with strong spin-polarization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided the missing boundary conditions in the diffusive regime for the case of strongly spin-polarised materials.
we have derived general boundary conditions for quasiparticle scattering in diffusive superconducting structures with strongly spin-pinned magnetic layers, including half-metallic feromagnets.

the boundary conditions for Usadel theory are derived in full generality and are applicable for any interface between two diffusive systems, including interfaces with strong spin-polarization and spin texture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proximity effect in the diffusive regime is qualitatively different from that in the ballistic regime, even for the case of strong spin polarization.

the Usadel equations are not sufficient for the description of proximity effects in diffusive superconducting heterostructures with half-metallic feromagnets, but that the quasiclassical equations of motion have to be supplemented by additional boundary conditions.
the Usadel theory is fully applicable to the study of proximity effects in heterojunctions between superconductors and strongly spin-polarised materials.
